venues.d: A private cliff-side mansion above the Atlantic, run as a home with one of Africa's great art and wine cellars.
The Pink Lady — Cape Town's grande dame since 1899, in nine acres of gardens below Table Mountain.
A marina-side resort with Table Mountain framed in the glass and a private spa island of its own.
A converted grain silo crowned with faceted glass, sitting atop the Zeitz MOCAA contemporary-art museum.
Laurence Graff's jewel of a wine estate on the Helshoogte Pass — art, diamonds and vineyards at altitude.

venues.n: Cape Grace, A Fairmont Managed Hotel
venues.d: A warm, quietly grand harbour house on its own quay, with one of the city's finest whisky bars.
A country-house hotel in nine acres of Constantia gardens — the calm, green, old-Cape antidote to the city.

venues.n: The Twelve Apostles Hotel and Spa
venues.d: A sea-facing house between mountain and Atlantic on the scenic road to Camps Bay — remote calm, minutes from town.
The Cape's oldest wine farm turned polished retreat — vineyards, a golf course and Cape Dutch calm.
The Royal Portfolio's flamboyant, art-filled manor on a private vine-and-olive estate in the valley.
An intimate boutique house in the heart of Franschhoek village — art, gardens and the main street at the door.
A legendary village inn reborn — the beating heart of Franschhoek's dining-and-village life.
A cluster of restored village cottages and suites with private pools, run with real warmth.
The old Reserve Bank turned grand city hotel — and the address that speaks Hindi at the door.
A restored Georgian-and-Victorian townhouse on a leafy Gardens street — a calm, characterful city base.
Cape Town's most celebrated kitchen — a treehouse-like room above Silvermist, and Africa's benchmark for fine dining.
Japanese precision married to South African produce — the only stand-alone African restaurant in Relais & Châteaux.
Chef Ryan Cole's seasonal cooking in a historic hunting lodge, with the Atlantic sweeping below.
La Colombe's Winelands sibling at Leeu Estates — theatrical tasting menus among the vines.
Waterside fine dining with table-side theatre and the ocean's finest produce at its centre.
An intimate, ambitious tasting-menu room that climbed to the very top of the Cape's rankings.
A Stellenbosch tasting-menu room that arrived at three stars almost fully formed.
Kobus van der Merwe's veldkos — foraged 'field food' from the strandveld, in a fisherman's cottage by the sea.
Buitenverwachting's elegant estate restaurant — refined cooking among the Constantia vines.
Small tapas-style plates on a mountainside deck with one of the Cape's great views.
Refined 'soigné' cooking in an approachable, everyday-elegant Constantia room.
Nic Charalambous's modern Greek-Cypriot — family recipes, Cape produce, and a buzzing Wale Street room.
Luke Dale Roberts's tapas-and-views room atop the Old Biscuit Mill — small plates, big city panorama.
Waterside fine dining with a light, produce-led hand and harbour calm.
A landmark wine-estate restaurant in a 300-year-old cellar — polished cooking and revered reds.
A spice-led tasting menu in the village — fragrant, considered, and quietly excellent.
A young-guns village kitchen doing sharp, seasonal cooking without ceremony.
A Stellenbosch tasting room that rose to the very top — precise, ingredient-led, personal.
One lunch, one dinner, no menu — a daily set feast of local, sustainable produce, cooked with heart.
Sustainably caught South African seafood from the Belly of the Beast team — sea-to-table and quietly serious.
Luke Dale Roberts's learning kitchen — training the next generation while cooking at a starred level.
An intimate neighbourhood room punching well above its size, on the slopes of the City Bowl.
Small plates at the water's edge below the Twelve Apostles — cooking and coastline in equal measure.
A pared-back, produce-first tasting room in the city — quiet, precise, ingredient-led.

venues.n: The Red Room by Chefs Warehouse
venues.d: The Chefs Warehouse group's intimate city room — small, sharing-led plates done with real polish.
A communal-table neighbourhood favourite where you eat what the chef feels like cooking.
Small plates and vineyard views at a Franschhoek wine estate — relaxed, generous, sharing-led.
Classic French technique in the village, from a chef with a devoted following.
Ángel León's Cape Town debut at the Mount Nelson — the 'chef of the sea', translated to the Atlantic.
The flat-topped mountain the whole city arranges itself around — take the rotating cable car up, and walk the summit while the Cape falls away on every side.
The island where Nelson Mandela was held for eighteen years, reached by ferry from the Waterfront and shown, movingly, by former prisoners themselves.

venues.n: Cape of Good Hope & Cape Point
venues.d: The dramatic, wind-carved southern tip of the peninsula — a funicular to the old lighthouse, cliffs plunging to two oceans, and the great sweep of the Cape at its wildest.
One of the world's great botanical gardens, set against the eastern slopes of Table Mountain, given over to the Cape's own fynbos and a treetop canopy walkway.
Stellenbosch and Franschhoek — Cape Dutch estates among the oldest in the New World, an easy hour from the city, best taken slowly over lunch and a tasting.
South Africa's oldest wine estate, producing since 1685 — a manor-house museum, historic cellars and a tasting of the sweet Constantia wines once shipped to Europe's courts.
The largest museum of contemporary African art, carved from a 1920s grain silo by Thomas Heatherwick — the continent's cultural landmark, and its most photographed interior.
A sheltered cove at Simon's Town where a colony of African penguins nests among the granite boulders — boardwalks bring you within arm's reach, without disturbing them.
One of the most beautiful coast roads on earth — a hundred and fourteen curves cut into the cliff face between Hout Bay and Noordhoek, the Atlantic straight below.
The candy-coloured Cape Malay quarter on the slopes of Signal Hill — cobbled streets, a living Muslim community, and the city's oldest surviving residential fabric.
The working Victorian harbour reborn as the Cape's front room — the ferry to Robben Island, Zeitz MOCAA, the Two Oceans Aquarium and the best of the city's shopping, all on the water.
The low ridge beside Lion's Head, where locals gather for sunset over the Atlantic — and where a cannon has been fired at noon, every day, since 1806.
The city's most-loved climb — a spiralling path to a 360-degree summit above the sea, walked at dawn, at sunset, and by the light of the full moon.
The full loop of the Cape Peninsula — Chapman's Peak, the Cape of Good Hope reserve, Simon's Town and Kalk Bay strung along one of the world's great day-drives.
The city's own vineyard belt, fifteen minutes from town — Groot Constantia, Klein Constantia and Buitenverwachting among leafy estates you can taste across in an afternoon.
A window onto the meeting of the cold Atlantic and warm Indian oceans — kelp forests, ragged-tooth sharks and a turtle rehabilitation programme, on the Waterfront's edge.
Drinks on the roof of the pillowed-glass Silo Hotel, above Zeitz MOCAA — the definitive Cape Town sundowner, Table Mountain on one side, the Atlantic on the other.
The Silo Hotel's double-height sixth-floor bar — teal banquettes, circular chandeliers and harbour views, the sheltered counterpart to the rooftop above.
Cape Town in a glass — fynbos, brandy and closed-loop, waterless technique from one of the country's most awarded bar teams, at the Waterfront and on Kloof Street.
A password-only speakeasy in a Victorian warehouse — velvet, mahogany and one of the city's most inventive cocktail lists, found by those who know to look.
At Cape Grace on its own quay — more than four hundred whiskies and a marina-side terrace, the city's most serious address for a dram.
Sundowners on a cliff-side lawn above the Atlantic, drawn from a nine-thousand-bottle cellar of South Africa's finest — arguably the most beautiful sundowner in the city.
Above the Camps Bay strip — the sun going down over the Atlantic, Lion's Head and the Twelve Apostles behind, cocktails and DJs as the beach empties.
The city's coolest block after dark — wine bars, cocktail haunts and pavement tables strung along a heritage street, the natural place to begin a Cape Town night.
The Mother City's historic nightlife spine — Victorian balconies, live music and clubs running till dawn, loud, mixed and unpretentious.
